headline: Third oil tanker in ~48h reportedly hits mine, catches fire (Sunday evening event, IRGC announcement early Monday)
dek: IRGC Navy says a tanker struck a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday evening, causing explosion and engine-room fire. Vessel had disabled positioning/navigation systems and was using the 'unauthorized southern route'.
sources: IRGC Navy Public Relations office (statement carried by Fars/IRNA/PressTV); maritime officials; UKMTO noted in Al Jazeera
fault_line: Who actually controls Hormuz: Iran's declared closure enforced with mines, or the US 'open for business' line? And is Iran mining its own gate, or chasing sanctions-evasion tankers?

sections.what_happened: IRGC Navy says a tanker struck a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday evening, causing explosion and engine-room fire. Vessel had disabled positioning/navigation systems and was using the 'unauthorized southern route'. IRGC warns any vessel deactivating navigation/identification systems 'will be dealt with severely and decisively'. Follows Saturday Oct 17 claims of two supertankers (each ~2M barrels crude) hitting mines. Al Jazeera live blog confirms IRGC video showing tanker ablaze.
sections.what_verified: Reuters Oct 17 carried the two Saturday claims (explicitly noting 'no independent confirmation'); Al Jazeera, Economic Times, Free Malaysia Today, Korea Times, Le Temps, PresTV carry Monday claim. Admiral Ali Ozmaei warning and AIS-off policy consistent across sources.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper (Friday) said 'the Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran' and 'remains open for business'; US naval counter-blockade on Iranian oil exports in place; no independent confirmation of mine incidents; Reuters explicitly flagged absence of independent confirmation for Saturday claims
sections.why_matters: Three tankers in 48 hours, one chokepoint, two competing realities. Map the mine claims, the AIS-dark runs, and the US counter-blockade side by side — then let the counterevidence sit on screen as long as the claim.
sections.context: Background: Strait of Hormuz — third oil tanker in ~48h reportedly hits mine, catches fire (Sunday evening event, IRGC announcement early Monday)

totw_analysis: Our read: Three tankers in 48 hours, one chokepoint, two competing realities. Map the mine claims, the AIS-dark runs, and the US counter-blockade side by side — then let the counterevidence sit on screen as long as the claim. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who actually controls Hormuz: Iran's declared closure enforced with mines, or the US 'open for business' line? And is Iran mining its own gate, or chasing sanctions-evasion tankers?
